# Incident Report — STRRAT RAT Infection

**Evidence:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 frames, 11.3 MB, capture span 2024-07-30 06:38:48 – 06:48:34 +0400, 585.7 seconds). No separate IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence folder; analysis is based entirely on the packet capture.

## Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.16.1.66** |
| MAC address | **00:15:fa:50:6f:18** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** (workgroup name broadcast as `WIRESHARKWORKSH`; AD domain `wiresharkworkshop.online`) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **ccollier** |
| Host OS (self-reported in malware beacon) | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit, Windows Defender as sole AV |
| Domain controller on the LAN | 172.16.1.4, hostname WIRESHARK-WS-DC |

Identified from NBNS name registration, Kerberos `CNameString` (`ccollier`, `DESKTOP-SKBR25F$`), and DHCP/ARP-resolved Ethernet source on all traffic from 172.16.1.66.

## Malware Family

**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT/info-stealer), C2 protocol version **1.6**.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The literal ASCII string `STRRAT` appears as a protocol field in every beacon sent to the C2 server. Full decoded beacon format observed:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<base64 active-window-title>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<idle time>
```

This is STRRAT's known plaintext, pipe-delimited "ping" heartbeat format, sent in the clear (no TLS) over a raw TCP socket. Bot ID `1BE8292C` stayed constant across the entire capture. The base64 field decodes to the victim's active window title at beacon time, confirming STRRAT's active-window/keylogging telemetry feature (observed values: `Documents`, `Home`, `Pictures`, `Program Manager`, a PowerPoint file, "Fanad Head Lighthouse - Paint").

## Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-Control
- **C2 endpoint:** `141.98.10.79:12132` (raw TCP, plaintext protocol, no TLS)
- First contact: t=76.99s into the capture (frame 9066, SYN)
- Beacon cadence: ~5 seconds, continuous through end of capture (t=585.66s)
- No DNS lookup preceded the connection — the C2 IP is hardcoded in the malware
- Beacon exchange pattern: client sends 7-byte size-prefix frame (`"136\r\n\r\n"` style length header), then the pipe-delimited status/ping string; server ACKs only, no observed inbound command payload in this capture window

### Reconnaissance
- `GET /json/ HTTP/1.1` to **ip-api.com (208.95.112.1:80)** at t≈9106 — IP-geolocation self-check, a common malware environment/victim-profiling step (result reflected in the `US:United States` field of every subsequent beacon)

### Likely payload staging chain (behavioral — TLS-encrypted, so no file names or hashes were recoverable from this capture)
Sequence starting at t≈64s, ~9–13 seconds before the first C2 beacon:
- t=63.96s: DNS queries for `github.com` and `repo1.maven.org` fired within milliseconds of each other
- t=64.05s: TLS session to **github.com (140.82.113.3:443)** — small, ~9.9 KB total
- t=64.83s: TLS session to **objects.githubusercontent.com (185.199.110.133:443)** — ~833 KB transferred, SNI `objects.githubusercontent.com` (GitHub release/raw-content CDN — likely the payload retrieval)
- t=68.0s: three parallel TLS sessions to **repo1.maven.org (199.232.196.209:443)** — ~8.9 MB combined (Maven Central CDN — consistent with a Java loader pulling runtime dependency jars)
- t=340.5s: single small TLS session to **javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com (23.194.164.136:443)** — ~47 KB (Oracle Java download endpoint; consistent with STRRAT being a Java-based RAT)

All four of these sessions are TLS 1.2/1.3 with no cleartext HTTP visible, so **no downloaded file names or SHA256 hashes could be extracted from the capture**. The domains themselves (github.com, githubusercontent.com, maven.org, oracle.com) are legitimate infrastructure being abused for payload/dependency hosting — flag by destination + timing correlation to the C2 start, not by domain reputation.

### Not malicious (ruled out)
- All LDAP/Kerberos/SMB/DCERPC/SAMR traffic between 172.16.1.66 and the domain controller 172.16.1.4 is consistent with normal domain-joined authentication and directory activity; no lateral movement indicators observed.
- The large volume of TLS traffic to Microsoft telemetry, MSN, Bing, and Office endpoints is normal Windows/Office background traffic, unrelated to the infection.

## Summary
Workstation DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:15:fa:50:6f:18), logged in as domain user `ccollier`, was infected with **STRRAT v1.6**. Shortly after startup the host pulled a payload and Java dependencies via GitHub/Maven Central infrastructure (t≈64–68s), performed an IP-geolocation self-check against ip-api.com, and began continuous plaintext C2 beaconing to **141.98.10.79:12132** roughly every 5 seconds for the remainder of the capture, transmitting host ID `1BE8292C`, active window titles, and OS/AV fingerprint data.
